title: Formal verification example (generated result)
description: What the verifier produced for an example, written by examples/tools/build.py. Do not edit by hand. This is the flat result: format 1 as stored (every result recorded before format 2), and the view of format 2 that the pages are rendered from (examples/tools/result_format.py; format 2 itself is stored-result.schema.json).

advice.description: What a run under --gaps advised returns when it reaches gaps with no contract (lib/src/advice.rs).

text.description: The claim in words, as the verdict would state it.

jdk.description: The JDK the gaps of JDK members are about.

id.description: The gap's stable id, which a contract is filed under.

assumed.description: What --gaps assume would take the call to do: what a contract replaces.

template.description: The gap's block of the template.

refusedContract.description: Why the contract given for the gap (--contracts) was refused, with where it is.

counterexamples.description: The inputs on which a JVM refutes the contract given, when that is why it was refused (step 3c), at most 20.

expected.description: What the contract says the call does there.

closed.description: The gaps the proof reaches that a contract given with --contracts closes, by id.

outside.description: What the engine refuses whatever the contracts say: each kind with its first member and site, and how many sites.

templateFile.description: The file in the example's folder the whole template was copied to.

typedValue.description: A witness value with its Java type, exact, from jvmcontract's `--json` outcome.

name.description: The parameter's or component's name; among `inputs`, the harness's own name for the input (`this.baseMillis` for a component of the receiver).

value.description: A boolean; a number for byte, short and int, and for char its UTF-16 code unit; a string for long (decimal, exact past 2^53) and for float and double (Java's toString of the value, which reads back as the same value: `0.1`, `-0.0`, `NaN`, `Infinity`); an array of those; or null. Absent for a record, whose components give it.

components.description: A record's components in declaration order: the arguments of its canonical constructor.

from.description: In a call: the input the argument is, or for the previous version's arguments given by `previousArguments`, the expression over the inputs that computed it.

typedCall.description: A call of a method on a witness, as data: enough to make the call again without reading the text.

class.description: The class declaring the method, as Java names it, in that version's classes.

classFile.description: The class file the method was read from, relative to the root of that version's classes.

classFileSha256.description: The SHA-256 of that class file as the run built it; null when the runner could not find it.

classes.description: Which classes: the patched version (`after`) or the previous one (`before`).

descriptor.description: The method's descriptor, as in the class file.

receiver.description: An instance method's receiver: a record built by its canonical constructor from its components.

witness.description: For a regression or property proof through jvmcontract: the counterexample as data, read from the outcome's typed fields. Absent in results written before 2026-11-05 and from tools that do not give it.

inputs.description: The symbolic inputs the checker chose, typed, in the harness's order: `input` is their rendering.

foundInputs.description: The inputs as the checker found them, when `inputs` are the shrunk ones.

call.description: The patched version's call on the inputs.

previousCall.description: For a regression proof: the previous version's call, on the same arguments or those `previousArguments` computes from the inputs. Absent when they could not be computed.

statement.description: The statement a verdict is about, as data (step 2a of llm-dlc/loops/sound-verdicts.md, lib/src/statement.rs): a regression proof's ∀x ∈ D, A(x) ⇒ Obs(old, x) = Obs(new, x), or a property proof's ∀x ∈ D, A(x) ⇒ P(Obs(x)), with what the verdict rests on besides.

kind.description: `regression` (two versions compared) or `property` (one version against an assertion).

domain.description: D: the target's receiver and parameters as it takes them, with nullability and aliasing.

null.description: Whether null is among its values: never today (an array is a fresh array, a record one its constructor built).

maxLength.description: The longest array it is given, for an array.

components.description: A record's components, `name: type`, the symbolic inputs it is built from.

sharedArrays.description: Whether two array parameters may be one array: never today.

text.description: The domain as the proof line writes it.

assumptions.description: A: what an input must satisfy, or what the checker takes for granted, each with its basis.

basis.description: `stated` by the claim, made by how the `harness` builds the statement, the checker's (`engine`) semantics, a gap `assumed` under --gaps assume with nothing to show for it, or a contract for a gap that a JVM `tested` or that nothing has checked (`trusted`), under --gaps advised --contracts.

id.description: The gap's stable id, for a gap.

observations.description: Obs: what is compared or checked of a call.

arrays.description: The array parameters whose contents after the call are compared too.

unwind.description: The loop unwinding bound, checked by unwinding assertions; null when no checker ran.

maxArrayLength.description: The longest array an array parameter is given; null without one.

complete.description: Whether the search covered every execution of every input in the domain within the bounds: a proof's did.

used.description: Whether the tool's models of JDK classes (lib/models) were read.

digest.description: `sha256:` and the digest of every model's name and class file; null when unused.

jdk.description: The JDK's version, whose classes the checker read.

solver.description: The SAT solver: JBMC's --sat-solver, or the own checker's bundled CaDiCaL with its version.

gapMode.description: The gap mode of the checker the verdict comes from; null for JBMC. `advised` with the checker `none` is a run that stopped at the gap scan, before solving.

confirmation.description: What JBMC made of the own checker's proof under --confirm; null when not asked for.

vacuity.description: A verified statement's only (step 2b): whether some input in the domain satisfies the assumptions and reaches the calls. Absent for another verdict, or from a tool from before it said.

status.description: `non-vacuous`: some input reaches the calls; `vacuous`: none does, so the proof covers no input; `unknown`: the probe gave no verdict.

basis.description: How it is known: `harness` (nothing skips an input before the calls), `probe` (the harness with the calls replaced by a failure, run by the tool's own checker), `identical` (the versions' bytecode is identical).

text.description: The status in a sentence, as the page states it.

witness.description: An input that reaches the calls, as the probe found it.

verdict.description: What the verifier concluded about the change: it shows a violation, it verified the claim, or it cannot be verified (the tool's own 'cannot be verified', with the reason in `problem`). Null when the run did not complete (see `execution`): only a completed run has a verdict.

execution.description: How the verifier's run ended, decided before anything in its output is read as a verdict. Absent in results written before 2026-11-05, every one of which completed. A violation needs a completed run and the evidence that shows it (a counterexample, a changed case, a capability or boundary change, a new `!` line, a model trace) and the verifier's report; an exit code of 1 without them is `invalid-output`.

status.description: `completed`: the verifier finished and said what it found. `timed-out`: it did not finish in the time allowed (the runner's, or TLC's within the tool). `killed`: a signal ended it (the out-of-memory killer's SIGKILL above all). `invalid-output`: it finished, but its output shows no verdict the runner can read (nothing printed, a violation with no counterexample, a missing report, JSON that is not a result). `tool-error`: the tool failed (an exit code it does not use for a verdict, a TLC run that ended without one).

exitCode.description: The process's exit code; negative for a signal; null when the runner stopped it.

reason.description: Why the run did not complete, in a sentence; null when it did.

expectation.description: Whether the result is the one example.json expects: `yes`, `no`, or `not-evaluable` when the run did not complete and so has no verdict to compare. `matchesExpected` is true exactly when this is `yes`. Absent in results written before 2026-11-05.

verdictLabel.description: The verdict with the approach's own measure of it, as shown in the tables: '✗ Violation: 2 of 36 cases changed', '✓ Verified: equivalent on every input'.

existingTests.description: The module's existing unit tests, run against the patched code: would they have caught the change without the verifier?

before.description: The changed region before the patch, with context.

after.description: The changed region after the patch, with context.

casesTotal.description: Size of the input domain when it is finite (B8), or null.

domain.description: The input domain in words when it is not finite (B9), for example 'priceCents: long × seats: int'.

counterexamples.description: Inputs whose outcome differs: from the contract (B8), or between the old and new version (B9, where 'contract' is the old outcome and 'actual' the new one). Each is a concrete, replayable witness.

contract.description: Null when the input is new.

actual.description: Null when the input no longer exists.

expected.description: For a property proof with throws clauses: what the property requires on this input, when that is what the method failed to do (the exception a clause declares, or a result where no clause applies).

found.description: For a regression or property proof through jvmcontract: the input as the checker found it, when `input` is the shrunk one.

shrinkRuns.description: For a regression or property proof through jvmcontract: how many smaller inputs the interpreter tried while shrinking the witness.

purityViolations.description: Why the method could not be proved pure.

trustedCalls.description: JDK APIs the proof trusted to be pure.

coverage.description: What the verdict rests on. For model checking (D1) through the tool: TLC counts how often a step of the model takes each row of the generated operators; a row no step takes is one the model says nothing about. For a regression or property proof through the tool: only whether the statement is vacuous, when no input in the domain reaches the calls.

oneOf.description: A regression or property proof through the tool that the tool reports as vacuous.

reason.description: The tool's `vacuously:` line: why no input reaches the calls.

status.description: How much of what the verdict rests on is known: `complete` when every configuration that counts coverage finished and TLC's statistics list every operator the verdict depends on (those with an altered row that decides, or all of them), `unavailable` when none lists any, `partial` otherwise. Only complete coverage can make a verdict vacuous. Absent before 2026-11-05, when coverage that was not read counted as no row taken.

fromRuns.description: The configuration explores runs from an initial state; false for an inductive step, which starts from every state the invariant admits.

finished.description: The run explored the whole model; a run that stops at a counterexample has partial counts, which are left out.

counted.description: The configuration counts coverage; false for one that cannot (the recorded runs: TLC attributes none to a next-state relation evaluated as an action property), which the page leaves out.

verdict.description: TLC's verdict on the configuration, or null when its run did not complete (absent before 2026-11-05).

status.description: How the configuration's run ended, as `execution.status` (absent before 2026-11-05).

reason.description: Why the run did not complete, or null.

coverageStatus.description: What is known of this configuration's coverage: `complete` when TLC's statistics list every generated operator, `partial` when some, `unavailable` when none, when the run did not finish, or when the configuration counts none.

coverageReason.description: Why the coverage is not complete, or null.

listed.description: The operators TLC's statistics list under an action of this run: the only ones whose counts mean anything.
TLC's statistics list the operator under an action; when false its counts are unknown, not zero (absent before 2026-11-05).

never.description: The rows no step takes, each as `case => outcome`.

changedRows.description: The rows of the contract the change alters (empty when the change was not meant to alter behaviour), each with the configurations whose steps take it.

symbol.description: The operator the row belongs to (absent before 2026-11-05).

unknownUnder.description: The configurations whose run finished but whose coverage statistics do not list the row's operator: whether they take the row is not known (absent before 2026-11-05).

nullRows.description: Rows with a null argument the change alters; the model leaves them out, since the protocol never passes null.

vacuous.description: Every run finished, the coverage is complete, and no run from an initial state takes any row the change alters that decides (rows that throw are meant never to be taken): the verdict is about the model as it was.

newProblems.description: For a boundary contract (B12) of an intended change: the `!` lines of the regenerated contract that the old one did not have. Each is a problem the change introduced, and makes the verdict a violation.

contractDiff.description: For an intended change: the diff of the regenerated contract, which is what a reviewer approves. For model checking (D1) of a change that is not meant to alter behaviour: the diff of each generated operator's contract the patched code changed anyway (the unauthorized difference in `modelContracts`), or null when there is none.

proof.description: One line on how the verdict was reached, from the verifier: the prover, what it covered, how long it took.

search.description: For a regression proof through jvmcontract (B9 on Quorum, Crosscut and Mica): the checker run the verdict comes from, read from `equivalence --json`; for a property proof, each property's own, under `properties`. Null when no checker ran (identical bytecode, a refusal before the search) or the run did not complete; absent in results written before 2026-11-05.

engine.description: `jbmc`, or `native` for the tool's own bounded model checker.

checker.description: The checker as the proof line names it: `JBMC 6.11.0`, or the own checker with its SAT solver.

seconds.description: From the first engine and input range tried to the verdict.

properties.description: The properties the checker proved or checked (JBMC's count; one for the own checker).

maxArrayLength.description: The bound on the length of an array parameter.

stage.description: The input range of the run the verdict comes from, as `[0:20]`; null for the whole range.

sharedCallees.description: The callees taken as one function in both versions, as `Class.method`.

fallback.description: Under `--engine auto`: why the own checker gave no verdict before JBMC was run.

gapMode.description: The gap mode the own checker ran under (`--gaps`), when the verdict is its: `strict`, `assume` or `advised`. Absent in results written before 2026-11-05.

gaps.description: The gaps the own checker met, constructs it does not implement as the JVM does (lib/src/bmc/gaps.rs): each `refused` (strict: the path that reached it ended there) or `assumed` (its approximation taken, which a verified verdict rests on).

id.description: The stable id: kind and member, with the JDK's version for a JDK call, as `jdk-constructor:java.util.ArrayList.<init>(I)V@jdk-25.0.4.1`.

call.description: The member as Java writes it.

approximation.description: What the own checker takes it to do under `--gaps assume`.

treatment.description: `refused` (the path ended there), `assumed` (its approximation taken), or closed by a `contract` (--contracts, applied at the call).

contract.description: For a gap a contract closed: what it states, who wrote it, what backs it, and where it is. The evidence is `tested` when a JVM ran the JDK's call on boundary and seeded random inputs and none refutes it (step 3c of llm-dlc/loops/sound-verdicts.md), else `trusted`, with why the JVM could not test it.

testing.description: What the JVM test found: the inputs inside `assume:` run to their end, how many returned and threw as each clause says, those outside `assume:`, those that ran out of the test's memory, the seed, the JDK, and the receiver an instance method was called on.

expected.description: What the contract says the call does there.

untested.description: Why the JVM could not test it, for a trusted contract.

file.description: The contracts file, as the tool was given it.

native.description: The own checker's account of its search, when the verdict is its: the numbers of its summary line (paths, merges, solverCalls, solvingSeconds, gatesEvaluated, evaluatingSeconds, divisions, divisionsBuilt, multiplications, multiplicationsBuilt, variables, clauses, seconds).

replay.description: For a regression proof's violation: where the checker's witness was run again on both versions, which a page says rather than assumes; for a property proof, each refuted property's own, under `properties`, the witness run on the method. Null otherwise; absent in results written before 2026-11-05, whose proof line says where.

by.description: `interpreter`: jvmcontract's own bytecode interpreter, not a JVM. `jvm`: the Box Office Java verifier, on the JVM.

reproduced.description: Whether the replay showed the disagreement the checker found; when it did not, the verdict is unverifiable. For a property, whether the interpreter's run showed the property failing: false too when the property calls the method under proof, which only the harness can evaluate, so that the violation is the checker's word.

advice.description: Under --gaps advised (approach.gaps), when the proof reached gaps of the tool's own checker with no contract and stopped before solving: each gap with what a contract for it must state, and a template (lib/src/advice.rs, step 3a of llm-dlc/loops/sound-verdicts.md). The template is copied to `templateFile` in the example's folder. Null otherwise; absent in results written before 2026-11-06.

stated.description: The statement the verdict is about, as data ($defs/statement). Null when the run built none or did not complete; absent in results written before 2026-11-06.

problem.description: Why the verifier refused, when the verdict is unverifiable and it is not a purity violation.

statement.description: File name of the statement the prover checked, such as a generated harness, relative to the example folder.

trace.description: For a model-checking violation (D1): the counterexample, one step per entry, with the action and the variables it changed.

statesExplored.description: For model checking (D1): the number of distinct states TLC explored.

invariant.description: For a model-checking violation (D1): the invariant or property that failed (`Deadlock` for a deadlock).

violationKind.description: For a model-checking violation (D1): what `invariant` names: an invariant, a deadlock, an action property (such as the next-state relation of a specification the model implements) or a temporal property (liveness).

forever.description: For a temporal violation (D1): how the counterexample goes on after its last step; TLC's counterexample is infinite, a prefix and then stuttering or a loop back into the prefix.

configurations.description: For model checking (D1) of a model with several configurations: one entry per TLC run, the model's own `.cfg` first, then the others (other constants, a symmetry set, an inductive check). The verdict and trace above are those of the first configuration that fails, else the first.

cfg.description: The configuration file, relative to the app.

verdict.description: TLC's verdict on this configuration; `unverifiable` when the run did not complete, with the reason in `status` and `summary`.

status.description: How this configuration's run ended, as `execution.status` (absent before 2026-11-05).

reason.description: Why this configuration's run did not complete, or null (absent before 2026-11-05).

summary.description: The run's one-line verdict, as the README's table shows it.

checkpoints.description: For model checking (D1) through the tool: where each configuration's TLC result came from. Each completed run is kept as soon as it completes, under the SHA-256 of everything it depends on (the model's modules and configurations, the generated operators and recorded runs among them, the standard modules, the command, jvmcontract, TLC's jar and Java), and is reused only when that fingerprint and its inputs match. Absent before 2026-11-05.

fingerprint.description: The inputs' SHA-256, or null when the configuration could not be set up.

reused.description: The result is an earlier run's with the same fingerprint, not one this run made.

recordedAt.description: When a reused result was recorded.

modelContracts.description: For model checking (D1): how each operator the model generates is tied to the patched bytecode. The operator is always generated from the contract derived from the patched classes in the run, and `behaviourChangeIntended` decides only whether a difference from the committed contract is allowed. A result recorded before this field existed generated the operator from the committed contract unless the change was intended.

symbol.description: The method the operator is generated from (`pkg.Class#method`).

contract.description: The contract file, relative to the app's root.

operator.description: The TLA+ module the operator is written to.

connection.description: `verified`: the contract derived from the patched classes is the committed one, so the patched code still behaves as the committed contract says. `derived`: it differs, and the operator comes from the derived one.

rowsChanged.description: The cases whose outcome differs between the committed and the derived contract, a new or removed case included. An outcome that differs only in its reason counts.

allowed.description: Whether the difference is allowed: no case changed, or the change is meant to alter behaviour. A case changed without that is a refuted obligation of its own, and the verdict is a violation whatever TLC found.

modelVerdict.description: For model checking (D1): TLC's verdict on the patched operators. `verdict` is this, except that a contract changed without an intended behaviour change makes it a violation.

modelSummary.description: For model checking (D1): TLC's own one-line verdict, the `verdictLabel` the run would have without `modelContracts`.

property.description: For a property proof (B11): the assumption (the inputs the property is about, or null), the assertion that was proved or refuted (null when the property is its throws clauses alone), and the throws clauses (`<exception> when <condition>`: the method throws that exception exactly where the condition holds). When the target has several properties, the headline one's (see `properties`).

properties.description: For a property proof (B11) through jvmcontract: every property the module declares for the target, in the order of its properties file, each with its own outcome and evidence, read from `prove --json`. Every one is required: the result's verdict is a violation when any is refuted, verified only when all are, and unverifiable otherwise. The flat `property`, `domain`, `proof`, `problem` and `statement` are the headline property's (the first refuted, else the first unresolved, else the first), and `counterexamples` holds every refuted property's witness. Null when the run did not complete; absent in results written before 2026-11-05, which kept one property's text.

harness.description: The tool's work directory of this property (`property-N`, N its place among the target's properties), when the target has several; null for one, whose harness is the work directory's own.

assert.description: The assertion as checked; null when the property is its throws clauses alone.

throws.description: The throws clauses as checked, the exception named in full.

vacuous.description: Why the property's proof covers no input (the tool's `vacuously:` line), or null.

counterexample.description: The refuted property's witness, as in `counterexamples`.

statement.description: The file the property's harness was copied to, `statement-N.java`, when the target has several; null for one, whose harness is `statement`.

stated.description: The property's statement, as data; absent in results written before 2026-11-06.

advice.description: The property's advice under --gaps advised, when its proof stopped at gaps with no contract.

stateMachine.description: For a state machine contract (B8, D1): the machine the patched code implements, as a Mermaid diagram.

claim.description: What the run checked, frozen before it ran (written to the attempt's directory as claim.json before anything was built). Another input or scope is another claim, with another id; another engine, timeout or tool is another attempt at the same one. Absent in results written before 2026-11-05 (step 3b of llm-dlc/loops/build-orchestration.md).

id.description: The first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the rest of the claim, canonical JSON.

statement.description: What is checked, as build.py's plan() states it: the approach, the target and its file, behaviourChangeIntended, and for B9 the intended inputs, previous symbol and arguments, and result relation.

scope.description: What a symbolic proof's statement is over (B9, B11): the array bound (null: the tool's default) and, for B9, the intended inputs the proof leaves out. Narrowing them is another claim.

inputs.description: The inputs' fingerprints: the patch's SHA-256, the files the run copies before and after the patch (the app's sources, contracts, models and build files, and for Box Office the Java verifier; build output left out), how dependencies are pinned, and for D1 the model's specification and configurations as the patched copy has them.

dependencies.description: `the JDK` for the javac apps; `declared in the build files` for Box Office, whose libraries Gradle resolves by the versions its (fingerprinted) build files declare, the artifacts themselves not fingerprinted.

model.description: D1: each model file, repo-relative, with its SHA-256.

attempt.description: The run as one attempt at the claim. Absent before 2026-11-05.

id.description: When it started (UTC) and 8 random hex digits.

claim.description: The id of the claim it is an attempt at.

seconds.description: From the claim being frozen to the result: the build, the tests and the verifier.

engine.description: The checker that decides a B9 or B11 verdict: `jbmc`, `native` or `auto`; null for the other approaches.

options.description: The flags jvmcontract's proof was given (plan()'s options).

tools.description: Each tool the plan names, by its identity: Java, javac and JBMC by the first line of their version, Gradle by the wrapper's distribution, jvmcontract and TLC by the SHA-256 of the executable or jar. Null for one that could not be asked.

bytecode.description: The classes the attempt built from the claim's sources, by content: `after`, the patched app's main classes; `before`, the unpatched ones a B9 run compares them with (null for the other approaches).

pipeline.description: The verification pipeline's job the attempt ran in (VERIFY_JOB_ID, VERIFY_SOURCE_COMMIT, VERIFY_WORKDIR); null when it ran outside the pipeline.

stages.description: Every command the attempt ran, in order: its name, how it ended (`exited`, `killed` by a signal, `timed-out`, or `not-started`), the exit code, the seconds, and where its stdout and stderr were streamed, relative to the attempt's directory (not published: kept with the workspace). Absent before stage logs were kept.

workspace.description: Where the attempt's directory was kept, relative to the pipeline job's work directory (VERIFY_WORKDIR): its patched copy with the harnesses and the tools' work directories, its stage logs and stages.jsonl, and its evidence. The pipeline keeps the work directory of a job that does not pass. Null outside the pipeline, where nothing is kept.

exploration.description: B9 and B11 by jvmcontract: the loop unwinding and array bounds searched within, and whether the checker showed its exploration complete within them (true for a verified proof, which checks unwinding assertions; null when unknown: a violation needs no completeness, and an unresolved proof has none).

conclusion.description: What the attempt concluded about the claim, per obligation. Absent before 2026-11-05.

status.description: `established` (verified), `refuted` (violation) or `unresolved` (unverifiable); null when the run has no verdict.

obligations.description: Each obligation checked on its own: a B11 target's properties, a D1 model's configurations and its generated operators' contracts as built. Empty when the claim is one obligation.

bundle.description: The evidence the attempt left, each file with its SHA-256 and size, published into the example's folder with result.json once both were checked; any other evidence file there is removed. A file that no longer matches its entry, or one the bundle does not list, is not this run's. Absent before 2026-11-05.

sarif.description: File name of the SARIF report, relative to the example folder; null when the verifier wrote none, which is never made up.

output.description: File name of the verifier's console output.
